entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Timur Khwaja was a Khan of the Golden Horde from 1361 to 1361.

In 1361, he briefly succeeded his father Khiḍr Khan as Khan of the Golden Horde and led the horde in its conquests across Eastern Europe.

As Khan, Timur Khwaja played a crucial role in the expansion of the Golden Horde's territories, which stretched from the Volga River to the Black Sea.

His reign had significant consequences for the region, including the destruction of several cities and the displacement of thousands of people.

The legacy of Timur Khwaja can be seen in the continued influence of the Golden Horde on the politics and culture of Eastern Europe during the Middle Ages.

"We have conquered and must conquer," he once said, "for we are the sons of Genghis Khan."
